transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Evan Cruz (Redwood CSM); Laura Chambers (CISO, Skyline), Ahmed Khan (VP Ops), Priya Nair (Cloud Security Engineer), Carlos Mendes (Infra Lead)
Shared artifacts: Redwood SLA deck (/redwood/security/SLA-deck.pdf), incident runbook template (shared in chat), SOC2 redacted link (will be posted), KMS integration diagram (to follow)

Summary: Quick review of incident response and BCDR procedures, RTO/RPO discussion and expectations for Skyline Bank. Walked through the escalation matrix and on-call process; covered what triggers an SLA investigation and the timeline for credits. Discussed encryption at rest, KMS options, and audit log retention. Plan: Redwood to send runbook + SLA metrics; schedule tabletop exercise.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you carving out time. I'm Jordan Lee, AE on the Skyline account, with Maya and Evan from the security and CS side. Laura, Ahmed, thanks for being here.
[00:16] Laura: Thanks Jordan. We'll keep this focused — Skyline is mainly concerned with RTO/RPO and how Redwood escalates during incidents.
[00:24] Maya: Hi all — Maya Patel, SE. I'll walk through our incident response flow, what our runbook looks like, and how we map incidents to SLOs/SLA. There might be a few notes where I say 'KV cache' and the transcript might show K-V or K V, apologies in advance.
[00:40] Ahmed: That's fine, just want to understand timelines — how quickly can we get a remediation or failover?
[00:47] Maya: For hosted API customers we have tiered responses: P1 is full outage, target initial response within 15 minutes, mitigation steps started within 30, and RTO target depends on whether you have Dedicated or Private. For Dedicated capacity customers we can aim for sub-5m warm failover if configured with HA groups and cross-zone replication; for hosted it's usually multi-region failover with RTO in the 10-30 minute range depending on KV cache warmup.
[01:15] Carlos: Wait — KV cache warmup, what does that mean for session consistency? If we fail to another region, will KV be lost?
[01:23] Maya: Good question. We persist KV snapshots regularly; there is a small window where in-flight KV could be lost unless you enable continuous streaming replication. For skyline, we recommended the continuous KV replicate option in Dedicated which reduces RPO to near-zero for most sessions. That option requires a config change and additional throughput, we can scope that.
[01:48] Priya: So RPO numbers — are you quoting N seconds or minutes? We need concrete numbers for our risk model.
[01:55] Maya: For Dedicated with continuous replication RPO is effectively 0-10s for token-level KV changes; for hosted it's normally 30-120s depending on load and region sync. Those are estimates; we'll back them up with test runs and a POC.
[02:12] Jordan: To clarify on SLAs — we provide a 99.95% uptime target for Dedicated contracts in the SLA doc. That includes a credit matrix. For hosted customers the SLA is lower by default; but enterprises often take dedicated. We'll send the exact SLA appendix after this call.
[02:28] Laura: And how are credits calculated? Is it prorated? Also what triggers an SLA investigation?
[02:34] Evan: Credits are tiered based on outage duration buckets — we log customer-impacting incidents and then do a post-incident review. An SLA investigation is triggered if we detect an outage that affects response codes or latency beyond the prescribed thresholds for 5 continuous minutes. We then run RCA, provide remediation, and calculate credits according to the contract.
[02:58] Ahmed: Who owns the pager on Redwood's side? I want names and levels so our SOC team can escalate.
[03:05] Jordan: We'll include a named on-call roster with escalation levels. Top-level: SE on-call -> Infra -> Engineering lead -> Exec on-call. Names rotate; we'll provide the rotation calendar and primary/secondary contacts.
[03:20] Laura: Also we need to see runbooks and playbooks. Not just high-level words.
[03:24] Maya: Yes — I uploaded a runbook template that shows actions for P1/P2, communication templates, and a timeline for RTO. It includes the step to notify customers via status.redwood.ai and Slack/email notifications.
[03:40] Priya: Can you walk through an example incident? Let's say region us-west goes down. What happens end-to-end?
[03:46] Maya: Sure — step one detection: internal probes and customer error reports. We declare Sev1 after the 3-minute threshold if both probes and customer errors are present. We fail traffic to us-east if it's a regional fault. For Dedicated customers with cross-zone replication, KV replay can start from replicated shard, replay prior KV within 30s. For hosted it's more like a rolling warmup. During failover we send a status page and open a customer incident ticket; we also run a hot rollback if needed.
[04:20] Carlos: Hot rollback — what's the risk to in-flight requests?
[04:25] Maya: There is a small chance of duplicate tokens or truncated responses; our client SDKs handle idempotency tokens but apps need to be tolerant. We'll document recommended client side patterns.
[04:38] Ahmed: On SLA credits — is there any cap? Like maximum credit per month?
[04:42] Jordan: Yes, the SLA document has caps and maximums, e.g., up to 50% credit for a single month depending on total downtime. We'll send the full schedule.
[04:52] Laura: Let's pivot to compliance artifacts — SOC 2 and ISO. We need redacted reports and lists of controls mapped to our control catalog.
[04:59] Jordan: We will share a redacted SOC 2 Type II report and an ISO summary. We'll also map our controls to common frameworks — we'll provide a matrix.
[05:10] Priya: On audit logs: retention, tamper-evidence, and who can access them. We need logs retained for 1 year, with tamper-evidence and RBAC controls.
[05:20] Maya: We keep request-level logs for 90 days by default and archived logs for up to a year on request. Logs are write-once in the archive and access is controlled via RBAC and KMS. We can provide a longer retention for dedicated contracts; that will be part of the SLA addendum.
[05:38] Carlos: Who has access to the keys in KMS? Are they customer-managed?
[05:41] Maya: For Private deployments or Dedicated with VPC, we support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-own-key). For hosted, we manage keys but we offer envelope encryption and HSM when needed. We'll share the KMS integration diagram.
[05:56] Ahmed: Key rotation cadence? Incidentally, what happens if a key is compromised?
[06:01] Maya: Rotation is configurable; default 90 days for root-like keys, 30-90 for data keys depending on policy. If a key compromise is suspected, we have a revocation and re-encryption plan; we perform an accelerated key roll and notify customers per the incident policy.
[06:17] Laura: On data residency — Skyline requires data to remain in-country for certain workloads. How do you support that?
[06:22] Jordan: We have region pinning and private deployment options. For in-country requirements we recommend Private or Dedicated with VPC peering in their region. We'll note any limitations for model variants that are not region-local.
[06:35] Priya: Do you support SSO/SAML and RBAC for admin access? We want SCIM and audit trails for admin actions.
[06:42] Evan: Yes — SSO (SAML/OIDC), SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. We log admin changes and those show up in audit logs. We'll include sample policies.
[06:54] Ahmed: For the escalation process, what's the timeline to get executive visibility? We need an escalation path that brings up an SLA owner within 30 minutes for P1s.
[07:02] Jordan: Exec escalation is configurable; our default escalation reaches exec on-call within 30 minutes for confirmed P1s. We can shorten that for enterprise customers in the contract.
[07:12] Laura: Tabletop exercise — can Redwood facilitate? We want a simulated incident so our SOC can practice.
[07:18] Evan: Absolutely. We run tabletop exercises with customers: staged incident, roles, and a post-mortem. We'll coordinate a date and provide scenarios.
[07:26] Priya: For proof — can you provide past incident timelines (redacted) so we can see typical RCA quality?
[07:31] Maya: We can provide a sanitized incident timeline and RCA examples. With names and sensitive items redacted. We'll include an example of a P1 RCA and remediation timeline.
[07:41] Carlos: A question on monitoring: how do you detect degraded latency vs complete outage? Do you use synthetic checks and customer metrics?
[07:47] Maya: We use combined synthetic probes, internal telemetry, and customer error rates. Degraded latency triggers a Sev2 typically unless error rates spike. We also provide per-route dashboards in the console for customers.
[08:02] Ahmed: Does Redwood do failover testing regularly? How often is DR exercised?
[08:06] Maya: We run internal DR drills quarterly and major full-region failover tests semi-annually. For Dedicated customers we can run customer-specific DR tests on a cadence agreed in the contract. We'll propose dates for Skyline.
[08:20] Laura: If an incident is caused by a third-party cloud provider outage, how does that affect credits and root cause?
[08:26] Evan: The RCA will note third-party contributions. SLA credits still apply if the outage causes customer impact under the contract's terms, though there are carve-outs for force majeure and provider-wide events depending on the contract language. We'll highlight those clauses.
[08:43] Jordan: Quick note on notifications — status.redwood.ai is our public status page. For customers we open a private incident channel (email + Slack + ticket) with updates every 10-15 minutes during active incidents.
[08:55] Priya: Can those notifications be pushed to our internal PagerDuty?
[08:58] Evan: Yes, we support PagerDuty integration and will provide a mapping for severity -> pager escalation.
[09:06] Laura: Onensics chain-of-custody — if we need to do forensics, do you preserve logs and snapshots?
[09:12] Maya: Yes we have a forensics preservation process; logs and container/shard snapshots are preserved in WORM storage when requested. That is part of the incident response playbook; we'll show examples.
[09:25] Ahmed: A note — be careful about broad access. We need proof that only necessary personnel can access devotion logs.
[09:31] Jordan: Understood, we'll include our RBAC maps and who has access to what.
[09:36] Maya: I'll note that audit trail entries include the admin id, action, timestamp, and justification field when required.
[09:44] Carlos: Any limitations on on-prem or air-gapped deployments for incident response?
[09:49] Maya: Air-gapped on-prem deployments require a local incident process — we provide the software and runbooks, but run-of-service is the customer's responsibility; Redwood provides remote advisory if allowed. For VPC/private deployments we can run support with cross-account roles.
[10:05] Laura: Final items — timeline and next steps?
[10:09] Jordan: Action items and next steps are in the chat but to recap: Maya shares the runbook and KMS diagram by Nov 7, Jordan sends SLA and historical uptime by Nov 8, Evan coordinates tabletop dates, Skyline to send on-call rotation. We'll post the SOC2 redacted link into the CRM.
[10:28] Priya: One last question — about model fallbacks and graceful degradation. If a heavy model causes latency spikes, what's Redwood's fallback?
[10:35] Maya: We have model variant fallback policies and automatic routing to smaller quantized variants when latency SLOs are violated. That can be configured per-tenant. We'll share the recommended policy for Skyline given their workload.
[10:48] Laura: Ok thanks — this is helpful. We'll review the runbook and SLA and come back with any redlines.
[10:53] Jordan: Great — thanks everyone. Evan will follow up on scheduling. We'll share artifacts in the CRM and chat.
[10:59] Ahmed: Thanks all.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Redwood: Share runbook, SLA appendix, SOC2 redacted report, KMS diagram, and sanitized incident RCA examples.
- Skyline: Provide on-call roster, confirm tabletop participants and preferred windows.
- Schedule tabletop week of Nov 17 (tentative).

End of transcript.
